svg.title: A decision tree for a server that does not appear in the host
svg.desc: Five questions stacked in a column on the left, each with an arrow to the right leading to the fix that applies when the answer is no, and a yes arrow leading down to the next question. In order: does it run standalone and hang, with the command to try; is every path in the configuration absolute, with an absolute path to uv as the example; is the configuration valid JSON with no byte order mark; was the host quit rather than merely closed; and is standard output nothing but protocol. The fixes name the traceback, the output of which uv or Get-Command uv, doubling backslashes and rewriting the file so it starts with 7B rather than EF BB BF, killing leftover host processes, and sending every log line to standard error. A yes on all five leads to the terminal box at the bottom, which says the host already wrote down what went wrong and gives its log path on Windows and on macOS.
svg.text: My server does not appear in the host
Work down the column. The first question you cannot answer yes to is your bug, and each one rules out a whole class of cause.
CHECK, IN ORDER
IF THE ANSWER IS NO, THE FIX
1. Does it run standalone, and hang?
uv run python -m system_info
no
Read the traceback. That is the whole problem.
No module named 'mcp': the dependencies are not installed.
yes
2. Is every path in the config absolute?
"command": "C:\\Users\\you\\.local\\bin\\uv.exe"
no
Paste the output of which uv, or Get-Command uv.
A graphical host does not inherit your shell's PATH.
yes
3. Is the config valid JSON, with no BOM?
BOM: a byte order mark, invisible in every editor.
no
Double every backslash, then rewrite the file without a BOM.
The first bytes must be 7B, not EF BB BF.
yes
4. Was the host quit, not just closed?
The config is read once, at startup, and never again.
no
Kill every leftover host process, then start it again.
A surviving process never re-reads its configuration.
yes
5. Is stdout nothing but protocol?
No print(), no banner, no debugger output.
no
Send every log line to stderr, and delete every print().
logging.basicConfig(stream=sys.stderr)
yes
All five clear? The host already wrote down what went wrong.
%APPDATA%\Claude\logs\mcp-server-system-info.log ~/Library/Logs/Claude/mcp*.log
